entityName: Consorzio MedITech - Mediterranean Competence Centre 4 Innovation
entityDescription:
MedITech (legal name Consorzio MedITech - Mediterranean Competence Centre 4 Innovation) is one of the eight Industry 4.0 Competence Centres established by the Italian Government. It was founded in 2020 by 8 universities and 22 industrial partners, and it is supported by an ecosystem of about 100 SMEs associated with the Competence Centre.
MedITech acts as a research and technology organisation (RTO) with the aim to foster the digitalization of the economy through technology transfer activities benefitting SMEs and public administrations. If focusses on key digital enabling technologies, notably 5G, IoT, cloud computing, machine learning, AR/VR/MR, and cyber-physical systems. It works in close collaboration with the other seven Competence Centres and the network of Digital Innovation Hubs to achieve national objectives while having a clear regional focus (with specific KPIs) on Southern Italy. This area is listed among the less economically developed in the EU, and MedITech acts as an enabler along with regional and national stakeholders to support convergence policies. MedITech is partner in three out of the 13 Italian EDIHs contributing skills and facilities through a targeted productised offer of digital solutions and “Test before Invest” services, with the aim to support the development of pre-commercial digital solutions.
MedItech has developed its test before invest strategy adopting digital assets as one of the main approaches to leverage the digitisation of SMEs. To this purpose it has set up a FIWARE Lab and a Big Data laboratory (adopting GAIA-X framework). The aim is to bring SMEs in its target geographical area closer to the adoption of open-source platforms for the development of smart solutions and to support them in the creation of business cases. At the same time, it is developing a rich training programme, leveraging resources from its founding members, to ensure the upskilling/reskilling of SMEs staff on the adoption and use of digital enabling technologies. 
MedITech is FIWARE Gold Partner. It is acting within its wider enterprise ecosystem as FIWARE evangelist through dedicated workshops and the promotion of business cases. In its network of associates, MedITech has identified several SMEs that already develop solutions using FIWARE and that are working collaboratively to create an enlarged community that will use FIWARE platform in their businesses.
In addition to a mandate to enable the growth of SMEs through the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies, MedITech has a duty to support the digitisation of public administration services. In this sense, it is already working closely with a few Municipalities in the framework of EU funded projects, facilitating their efforts in the adoption of big data-based solutions for smart city and mobility applications.

About DLR - Cutting-edge research from fundamental principles through to applications. DLR is the Federal Republic of Germany's research centre for aeronautics and space. It combines its scientific work and technological developments in these areas with its expertise in energy, transport, security and digitalisation. The German Space Agency at DLR plans and implements the national space programme on behalf of the federal government. Two DLR project management agencies oversee funding programmes and support knowledge transfer.
Climate, mobility and technology are changing globally. DLR uses the expertise of its 55 research institutes and facilities to develop solutions to these challenges. Our 10,000 employees share a mission – to explore Earth and space We conduct research and development activities in the fields of aeronautics, space, energy, transport, security and digitalisation. The German Space Agency at DLR plans and implements the national space programme on behalf of the federal government. Two DLR project management agencies oversee funding programmes and support knowledge transfer. and develop technologies for a sustainable future. In doing so, DLR contributes to strengthening Germany's position as a prime location for research and industry.

Locations
In total, DLR has 34 locations: Cologne (headquarters), Aachen, Aachen-Merzbrück, Augsburg, Berlin, Bonn, Braunschweig, Bremen, Bremerhaven, Cochstedt, Cottbus, Dresden, Geesthacht, Göttingen, Hamburg, Hanover, Jena, Jülich, Kiel, Lampoldshausen, Neustrelitz, Oberpfaffenhofen, Oldenburg, Rheinbach, Stade, St. Augustin, Stuttgart, Trauen, Ulm, Weilheim and Zittau. 
DLR also has offices in Brussels, Paris, Tokyo and Washington D.C.
Locations and offices in Germany and abroad: https://www.dlr.de/en/dlr/locations-and-offices

DLR is managed by its Executive Board. Since October 2020, Prof. Dr.-Ing. Anke Kaysser-Pyzalla has been Chair of the Executive Board, while Klaus Hamacher is Vice Chairman. The Executive Board also includes Prof. Dr. Karsten Lemmer, responsible for the Executive Board department "Innovation, Transfer and Research Infrastructure", and Dr. Walther Pelzer, responsible for the "German Space Agency at DLR" based in Bonn.

entityDescription: GeSiM was founded 1995 as a spin-off from the Rossendorf Research Center. The company is a non-public and privately held entity. Building upon a broad expertise in micromachining technologies, GeSiM has evolved into a bioinstrumentation company focusing on submicroliter liquid handling instruments and microfluidics. GeSiM is specialized in liquid handling automation, microfluidics and micro contact printing. As a leading supplier of submicroliter dispensers GeSiM developed a unique design for piezoelectric pipetting tips, based on silicon-glass chips. The benchtop pipetting system Nano-Plotter runs up to 16 of these accurate dispensers and is mainly used as non-contact arrayer for microarrays, biochips and biosensors. Liquid handling by contact printing is available with the GeSiM micro-contact printers. These instruments transfer sample into tiny 2-dimensional patterns or generate 3-dimensional structures by Nano-Imprint-Lithography (NIL). Recent developments are focused on instrumentation for 3D printing of biocompatible materials, e.g bioscaffolds. Common 3D printers are usually not capable of processing biocompatible materials. The latest development is a compact synthesis station for radiochemistry, which combines liquid handling, solids handling, reaction engineering. These systems perform autonomously radio synthesis in commercial available hotcells on the basis of the GMP standards. Micro structuring methods are used to manufacture miniaturized fluidic components from silicon, glass, ceramics and PDMS to create products which cannot be made by conventional methods. GeSiM's specialty is the ability to offer complete tailor-made solutions to customers, including not only microfluidics, but also packaging, mechanics, macrofluidic engineering, and specialized control software (World-Chip Interface.

entityDescription:
Norbite upcycles plastic waste into sustainable goods.

Norbite has developed a disruptive approach towards end-of-life polymeric materials for which there is no viable re-use or recycling solutions. Based on one specific insect,Galleria mellonella, the developed scalable process enables the insects to digest and transform plastics into proteins, lipids and biofertilizers.
Instead of disposal or incineration, the conventional end-of-life scenario in a linear plastic value chain, Norbite develops the technological and commercial foundations to allow residual polymeric materials e,g, packaging, textile, furniture, to be utilised as a food source for G. mellonella. As the larvae of the insect are refined for multiple high-value products, aimed to food & feed, and organic farming applications; the utilisation of plastic waste in this way gives it the opportunity to re-enter the economy.
The insect’s transformation capabilities mean the elimination of residual products in the plastic industry through their conversion into input material for another value-creating one i.e. industry symbiosis.

entityDescription:
At INSIGHIO we accelerate IoT adoption, from conception to final product, with a unique application-agnostic hardware and software technology stack. We help third parties to overcome the technological entry barriers which prevail today and are slowing down the IoT uptake. Relying on an in-house developed technology integrating terrestrial and satellite connectivity and a fast-track IoT applications design and implementation service, we solve one of biggest challenges in today’s new IoT projects, that is, the inadequate Proof-of-Concept during early stages. Thanks to a flexible and modular hardware, which is backed by a fully customizable firmware and Cloud software, INSIGHIO bridges the gap between prototyping and production, scaling an IoT deployment from a few nodes to hundreds of nodes, in a very short time frame. We foresee countless domains for our offering, e.g. precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, asset tracking, and alerting in remote oil, gas and construction industries.

We offer the following products & services:

- insigh.io Node: A generic IoT hardware device embedding multiple technologies used as a development board or in end applications
- insigh.io Platform: An end-to-end IoT software suite with many integrations taking care of all end-point and cloud functionalities
- insigh.io Service: A bundle of rapid IoT application design, prototyping and deployment, built on-top of the insigh.io stack

Our main customers are:

- Integrators & Solution providers who look for the core IoT building blocks
- Businesses in the need of IoT hardware/software to automate processes
- R&D groups requiring the proper IoT enablers to back their research work
- Any company/organization wanting to test a new IoT idea

A representative set of completed/ongoing projects are:
- Soil and environmental monitoring in remote farms for precision agriculture
- Beekeeping management optimization through beehives weight monitoring
- 24-h indoor air-quality assessment for smart post-COVID workspace control
- Connected weigh-scales to incentivize recycling and promote cyclic economy
